fixer.title: notebook: avoid quadratic carriage-return stream normalization

cases.mechanism: The old normalization loop repeatedly scanned, matched, replaced, and reallocated the entire accumulated stdout string once per carriage-return overwrite, making a multi-line progress batch scale approximately O(N*R), quadratic when record size is bounded.
cases.symptom: Large notebook stdout progress batches can synchronously stall output updates and delay renderer/event publication; the PR's production-path regression test uses 4,000 carriage-return records, where the old algorithm performs thousands of full-stream passes.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added line-wise replace processes each logical line once, splits only carriage-return-bearing lines, and walks their segments once from right to left. For ordinary streams this changes normalization from repeated whole-stream work per overwrite to work linear in the decoded bytes and carriage-return segments, while retaining the legacy fallback only for dollar-bearing overwritten lines.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, fixCarriageReturn's while loop handled one carriage-return overwrite at a time; each iteration re-matched and replaced against the whole accumulated decoded stream. NotebookCellOutputTextModel.appendData synchronously calls optimizeOutputItems -> compressOutputItemStreams before incrementing the version or firing onDidChangeData, and the notebook text model emits the output-item event only afterward. The new 4,000-record model test demonstrates a realistic batch cardinality on this path. Thus R overwrite records in N bytes caused repeated whole-string scans and allocations on the notebook output update critical path.
